candidates.title: Boat trip around Percé Rock and Bonaventure Island
candidates.summary: Covers the requested Percé Rock stop: a boat circles the rock and lands on Bonaventure Island, home to a huge northern gannet colony, with an easy trail suited to kids 7 and 11. Access needs were not answered, so trail and boarding accessibility is unaccounted for.

candidates.title: Cap Gaspé walk in Forillon National Park
candidates.summary: Covers the requested Forillon stop: a moderate coastal trail to the lighthouse at Land's End, with chances of seals and whales. Distance may be long for a 7-year-old; access needs not answered.

candidates.title: Grande-Grave heritage site, Forillon
candidates.summary: Restored fishing-village buildings with easy walking and family-friendly interpretation; a short, low-effort stop that breaks up driving.

candidates.title: Reford Gardens (Jardins de Métis)
candidates.summary: Large historic gardens on the south-shore route, a good leg-stretch stop for the kids on the way out or back. Accessibility not accounted for.

candidates.title: Miguasha National Park fossil site
candidates.summary: UNESCO fossil site on the Baie-des-Chaleurs side of the loop, new to a family who has done the north shore; museum and beach walk appeal to an 11-year-old.

candidates.title: Exploramer sea museum
candidates.summary: Hands-on marine museum with touch tanks, a kid-pleasing stop along the north Gaspé coast road.

candidates.title: Short hike in Parc national de la Gaspésie
candidates.summary: An easy-to-moderate trail near the Gîte du Mont-Albert, with a chance of seeing moose or caribou country; pick a short loop for the 7-year-old. Accessibility not accounted for.

place.name: Parc national de la Gaspésie, Gîte du Mont-Albert area

candidates.title: Site historique du Banc-de-Pêche-de-Paspébiac
candidates.summary: Historic fishing-industry buildings on Baie-des-Chaleurs with family activities; a gentle stop on the southern half of the loop.

candidatesAccepted.title: Highway 20 east along the south shore to the lower St. Lawrence
candidatesAccepted.summary: First leg out of the city on the south shore, which keeps you off the north shore you've already done. Break it at a rest area so the 7-year-old gets out of the car before the three-hour mark. Access needs were not answered, so stop accessibility isn't accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Lower St. Lawrence coast drive on Route 132
candidatesAccepted.summary: A coastal drive with frequent pull-offs, such as Le Bic, so stops can be short and often. The duration has not been measured.

candidatesAccepted.title: Haute-Gaspésie north coast road on Route 132
candidatesAccepted.summary: The dramatic cliff-and-village stretch of the peninsula, with many small harbours to stop at. Some sections are winding. The duration has not been measured.

candidatesAccepted.title: Around the tip of the peninsula on Route 132
candidatesAccepted.summary: A short leg connecting the two stops you already want. Short enough for a 7-year-old. The duration has not been measured.

candidatesAccepted.title: Baie des Chaleurs south coast drive on Route 132
candidatesAccepted.summary: The return side of the loop, with calmer beaches and towns such as Bonaventure and Carleton-sur-Mer. The duration has not been measured, so it may need splitting.

candidatesAccepted.title: Matapédia Valley crossing back to the St. Lawrence
candidatesAccepted.summary: An inland river-valley route that closes the loop without repeating the north coast. The onward run to Montréal would need further legs that each fit within the daily limit. The duration has not been measured.

candidatesAccepted.title: Camping in Forillon National Park, Petit-Gaspé
candidatesAccepted.summary: Serviced Parks Canada campground with showers, close to trails and beaches in Forillon; fits a simple roughest night for a family of four. Access needs were not answered, so check site accessibility. July sites go fast once Parks Canada reservations open.

candidatesAccepted.title: Family motel in Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple motel or motel-style inn in Percé puts the family within walking distance of views of Percé Rock and the Bonaventure Island boats. Rooms that sleep four are scarce in July. Access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Camping at Parc national du Bic
candidatesAccepted.summary: SÉPAQ campground with shower blocks, a short drive off the highway near Rimouski. It breaks the long run from Montréal into shorter legs for the seven-year-old, and it sits on the south shore rather than the north shore they have already seen.

candidatesAccepted.title: Ready-to-camp tent at Parc national de la Gaspésie
candidatesAccepted.summary: A SÉPAQ ready-to-camp tent or cabin near Gîte du Mont-Albert, inland in the Chic-Chocs. It is simple and has beds, so there is no gear to haul, and showers are nearby. It gives the loop an inland mountain stop. Access needs were not answered.

place.name: Parc national de la Gaspésie, Mont-Albert sector

candidatesAccepted.title: Motel or cottage in Carleton-sur-Mer
candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple motel or rental cottage on Baie des Chaleurs for the southern leg of the loop. Beaches and Mont Saint-Joseph keep the kids busy, and the town gives a good rest point on the way back west.

candidatesAccepted.title: Motel in Matapédia valley (Amqui)
candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple motel in the Matapédia valley, inland, that closes the loop without retracing the coast. It splits the drive back toward Montréal into shorter legs.

candidatesAccepted.title: Smoked fish at a Gaspé Peninsula fish smokehouse
candidatesAccepted.summary: A family-run smokehouse in Rivière-au-Renard area near Forillon is a classic Gaspésie food stop; a kind of place, no premises named. Dietary restrictions and access needs were not answered, so check what the party can eat.

candidatesAccepted.title: Lobster or seafood shack in Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: Fresh Gaspésie lobster or fish and chips eaten near Percé Rock makes the meal part of the visit; a kind of place, no premises named. Dietary needs not answered; shellfish may not suit everyone.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bakery stop in Kamouraska
candidatesAccepted.summary: Kamouraska on the south shore breaks up the drive from Montréal with a bakery and riverside village stroll, good for a restless seven-year-old; a kind of place, no premises named. Dietary needs not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Fromagerie stop in the Matapédia Valley
candidatesAccepted.summary: A local cheese dairy on the inland return leg through the Matapédia Valley offers fresh curds kids enjoy and a new route for the loop; a kind of place, no premises named. Dietary needs not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon National Park camping (serviced campground with showers)
candidatesAccepted.summary: Des-Pionniers or Petit-Gaspé campgrounds have showers, so they stay inside the family's limit on shower-less nights; a family of four can base here for hiking, beaches and seal-watching. The band assumes one site per night for the party at Parks Canada rates and does not include the daily park entry fee. Access needs were not answered, so I could not check site or trail accessibility.

candidatesAccepted.title: Parks Canada family/group day pass for Forillon
candidatesAccepted.summary: Forillon charges a daily entry fee, and a family/group rate usually covers a car of four more cheaply than individual passes. The band is per day for the whole party. If they visit other Parks Canada sites in the same year, an annual Discovery Pass may cost less; I have not checked that against their route.

candidatesAccepted.title: Boat cruise to Percé Rock and Bonaventure Island
candidatesAccepted.summary: This is the classic way to see Percé Rock up close and to land among the gannet colony, and it suits moderate effort and children. The band assumes adult and child tickets for two adults and two children on a standard cruise, plus the Parc national de l'Île-Bonaventure entry fee. Access needs were not answered, so I could not check boarding or trail access.

candidatesAccepted.title: Motel or cabin night in the Matapédia Valley
candidatesAccepted.summary: The south-shore leg through the Matapédia Valley and Baie-des-Chaleurs is new to them, since they have done the north shore, and it breaks the long drive into shorter legs for the seven-year-old. A simple motel or cabin with a shower keeps camping nights in check. The band assumes one room or cabin for four in peak July, before taxes.
